summary: Niobium coplanar waveguide resonators are encapsulated with thin tantalum capping layers to suppress the lossy native NbOx surface oxide and replace it with a more uniform Ta2O5 interface. Fresh Nb/Ta bilayer devices achieve internal quality factors up to $2.4 	imes 10^6$ in the single-photon regime with reduced two-level-system loss compared to uncapped Nb controls, and remain superior after six months of storage despite moderate degradation.
motivation: Niobium's native Nb2O5 oxide is a dominant source of two-level-system loss in superconducting resonators, whereas tantalum forms a more stoichiometric and structurally uniform Ta2O5 with fewer defects, motivating hybrid Nb/Ta bilayers as a surface-engineering route to improve coherence without sacrificing fabrication maturity.
method: Eight $\lambda/4$ CPW resonators were fabricated on high-resistivity silicon with sputtered 165–175 nm Nb base layers and 25–35 nm Ta caps deposited in situ, alongside reference Nb-only devices using identical processing. Power-dependent transmission spectroscopy was performed at 10 mK to extract internal quality factors and decompose losses using a standard tunneling-model fit to $1/Q_i(\bar{n}) = 1/Q_0 + (1/Q_{\mathrm{TLS}})/(1 + \bar{n}/n_c)$.
result: Nb/Ta resonators exhibit $Q_{\mathrm{TLS}} \sim 4$–$10 \times 10^6$ (mean $\sim 7 \times 10^6$) compared to $Q_{\mathrm{TLS}} \approx 2.3 \times 10^6$ for fresh Nb-only devices; after six months, aged Nb/Ta devices degrade to mean $Q_{\mathrm{TLS}} \approx 3.5 \times 10^6$ but remain superior to baseline Nb, while background loss $Q_0 \sim 2.9 \times 10^6$ dominates over TLS contributions (60–80% of total loss).
